title: fallback-hunt-session-playbook-2026-03
content:
Fast scratchpad from on-call hunting session (personal notes). Goal: capture commands I ran, quick log excerpts, hypotheses, and a minimal playbook so I can hand off. Put in SRE postmortem later if we confirm a reproducer.

Summary/Context:
- Time window: 2026-03-11 16:04 - 18:20 UTC. Customer-facing reports: intermittent 503s for hosted API in eu-west-1 with automatic fallback to us-east-1 introduced latency spikes (~600-900ms extra). Smart routing should have routed to eu-west-2 first and then fallback to nearest compatible variant per policy, but traffic ended up hitting cross-region egress more than expected.
- Symptom: elevated 5xx rate (503/504) on model-serving proxies in eu-west-1 + a surge in cross-region egress from api-gateway -> us-east-1. Some requests also saw 429s at edge when rate limits bumped due to concurrent fallbacks.
- Impact: customer latency SLO breaches and increased egress/cost. No data exfil. No auth failures.

What I observed in the console/metrics:
- Per-route dashboard: route /v1/generate/eu reported 3.8% 5xx at peak between 16:15-16:40 UTC. Fallback_count metric spiked from baseline ~50/min to ~480/min.
- SmartRouting decisions table showed an unusual number of "no-capacity" decisions for eu-west-1 despite provisioned capacity for this tenant. Decision reason column returned "node-unhealthy" / "local-queuing-threshold" inconsistently.

Commands I ran (local) and outputs (copied raw where useful):
1) Quick check of routing decisions for a single request id (request-id: req-0a1b2c3d):
$ redwoodctl routing decisions get --request req-0a1b2c3d --format json{
  "request_id": "req-0a1b2c3d",
  "route": "/v1/generate/eu",
  "chosen": {"region": "us-east-1", "node": "gateway-eu-22"},
  "reason": "fallback_policy:regional -> capacity_unavailable at eu-west-1: node-unhealthy",
  "decision_trace": ["match-route", "check-region-capacity(eu-west-1)", "node-health-fail(eu-west-1:node-17)", "select-fallback(us-east-1)"]
}
Note: decision_trace implies routing service saw node health fail for a node in eu-west-1 and immediately selected us-east-1 fallback.

2) Inspect node health from node manager API:
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-node-mgr.redwood/api/v1/nodes?region=eu-west-1 | jq '.nodes | map(select(.id=="node-17"))'
[
  {
    "id": "node-17",
    "status": "degraded",
    "last_heartbeat": "2026-03-11T16:12:07Z",
    "restarts": 2,
    "cpu_util": 84,
    "gpu_mem_pct": 93,
    "queued": 12
  }
]
Observations: node-17 overloaded, high GPU mem utilization. But other nodes in eu-west-1 also showing high queued counts (7-12) around same time.

3) Check autoscaler logs (k8s cluster eu-west-1):
$ kubectl -n serving logs deployment/serving-autoscaler --since=2h | grep "scale" | tail -n 20
Mar 11 16:10: scaler: decision=scale_up reason=queued_increase target_replicas=6 current_replicas=4
Mar 11 16:11: scaler: decision=scale_up reason=scale_failed error=quota-exceeded cloud-quota=4 current=4
Mar 11 16:13: scaler: decision=retry reason=backoff next_attempt=16:17
Interpretation: autoscaler attempted to scale but cloud quota prevented rapid scale-up. That produced sustained queuing and eventually node status degraded.

4) Edge logs showing fallback event markers (snippet):
[2026-03-11T16:14:22.284Z] request=req-0a1b2c3d route=/v1/generate/eu client=acct-1123 decision=FALLBACK region=us-east-1 reason="node-unhealthy" latency_ms=1031 fallback=true
[2026-03-11T16:14:22.357Z] request=req-0a1b2c3d proxy=proxy-eu-5 upstream=us-east-1-res p50=92 p95=380 error_code=200
Note: initial hop had extra latency while connecting to cross-region upstream.

5) Rate limiter back-pressure evidence on edge:
$ curl -I -H "x-request-id: test-rl" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
x-rate-limit-used: 98
x-rate-limit-limit: 100
This shows rate limiter usage near limit for that account/route during fallback surge.

Hypotheses (rough prioritization):
- H1: Autoscaler in eu-west-1 couldn't scale due to cloud quota limits; nodes reached high GPU mem and started failing health checks -> routing service marked nodes unhealthy -> fallback to other regions. Evidence: scaler logs show quota-exceeded.
- H2: Healthchecker aggressiveness increased (recent change in https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/412) which lowered tolerance for queued/gpu-mem spikes, causing premature node-unhealthy labels. Evidence: MR changed node health thresholds on 2026-03-10.
- H3: Persistent asymmetric traffic (spike from a small set of tenants) overloaded region because routing sticky policy sent them to eu-west-1 preferentially; fallback cascade caused global ripple and rate limiter thrash across regions.
- H4: KV cache warm-up behavior: when fallback happened, requests lacked warm prefixes and caused longer serving latencies in destination region, amplifying perceived latency.

Quick checks to validate H2/H1:
- Reviewed PR 412 testcases: new check flags queue_length > 8 as unhealthy. At peak, some nodes had queued=12 so this would flip health. Old threshold was >16. So H2 plausible.
- Cloud quota: billing/infra noted eu-west-1 had vGPU quota at 4 extra instances; autoscaler tried to request 2 more but hit quota -> scale_failed. So H1 also plausible and probably root cause. H1+H2 interaction likely.

Immediate mitigation options (notes to self, safe to execute with SRE lead):
1) Reduce healthchecker sensitivity (roll back PR or toggle flag) to previous thresholds to avoid marking nodes unhealthy while autoscaler works through quota. Short-term config: health.node.queue_threshold=16 -> 32 (safe, but conservative).
2) Emergency quota request: open cloud quota request and request temporary burst. Already pinged infra. ETA 1-2h.
3) Temporarily increase fallback_policy grace window (so routing tries local region for extra duration before failing over) — reduces cross-region egress. But could increase tail latency if nodes are truly unhealthy.
4) Apply per-account rate limiter softening to avoid 429s during traffic bursts (bump limit for affected account) — requires careful guard rails.

Notes on commands to enact mitigation (ops playbook):
- Toggle health threshold via feature-flag service:
$ ffctl set routing.health.node_queue_threshold 16 --env prod --comment "temp revert after incident"
- To increase grace window:
$ redwoodctl config set routing.fallback.grace_window_ms 250 --env prod --who marissa
- To throttle cross-region egress at edge as last resort (reject before cross-region):
$ redwoodctl edge set-policy --route /v1/generate/eu --policy block-cross-region-fallback=true --expire 2026-03-13T00:00:00Z --who marissa
(Use with caution; will cause more local 503s if region truly unhealthy.)

Logs/snippets I copied for postmortem:
- autoscaler scale_failed lines (see above)
- node manager dump for nodes eu-west-1 nodes 12-22 during 16:10-16:20 (saved to /tmp/eu-nodes-dump-2026-03-11.log)
- routing decisions timeline (extracted to /tmp/route-decisions-reqs-16-20.json)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Who authorized PR 412 health threshold change? Pull request linked above shows small test coverage; need to ask @Ibrahim (collab) whether rollout included canary config.
- Autoscaler cloud quota: do we have a predictive metric to raise quota before region saturation? Consider autoscaler detecting quota-exceeded and circuit-breaking to reduce rate of new requests to avoid cascade.
- Can fallback policy be more conservative about cross-region egress cost (route by latency+cost + grace window) instead of immediate failover on node-unhealthy?

Next steps for handoff to SRE/infra (ordered):
1) Rollback/Tune health threshold flag (if SRE approves).
2) Confirm temporary quota increase with infra and monitor queue depth.
3) Re-run traffic replay against eu-west-1 small subset to ensure queue depth improves and fallbacks drop.
4) Add a routing canary that simulates temporary node-unhealthy scenarios to ensure PR changes don't flip too aggressively.

Notes-to-self (things I scribbled during the hunt):
- Avoid immediate global rollback of PR 412; opt for flag toggle first.
- Save all raw logs to /mnt/oncall_dump/fallback-2026-03-11 for PM and postmortem.
- Slack post summary draft: "Investigating increased cross-region fallbacks from eu-west-1; suspected autoscaler quota + health threshold change. Taking temporary flag revert and requesting quota bump. Will update in 30m."

If I forget anything: key artifacts saved -> /tmp/eu-nodes-dump-2026-03-11.log, /tmp/route-decisions-reqs-16-20.json, incident trace id bundle: trace-bundle-req-0a1b2c3d.tar.gz

-- end scratchpad --
